items.title: An AI programme inside a live logistics operation
items.challenge: Operations teams handling thousands of shipments a day, with institutional knowledge trapped in documents and in the heads of a few senior staff.
items.approach: Retrieval-augmented chatbots grounded in the company's own operational data, plus internal copilots used daily by operations teams.
items.result: Grounded answers from company data instead of guesswork, and repetitive internal questions answered without interrupting senior staff.

items.title: An AI receptionist that answers real phone calls
items.challenge: Businesses lose bookings to unanswered phones after hours, and generic voice bots hallucinate answers they cannot support.
items.approach: We built a multi-tenant SaaS bridging Twilio Media Streams to a real-time voice agent, with every answer grounded in that tenant's own documents.
items.result: Live calls answered around the clock with knowledge-grounded, hallucination-resistant responses — the same architecture behind dispatch and booking agents for logistics.

security.heading: Your shipment data is commercially sensitive. We treat it that way.
security.subheading: The objection we hear first from every logistics operator — answered up front.

items.title: Your data never trains a public model
items.body: Operational data, rates and customer records stay inside your boundary and are never used to train third-party models.

items.title: Grounded answers, or none
items.body: Agents answer from your records and cite the source. When there is no grounded answer, they say so and hand off — they don't invent one.

items.title: PII and commercial redaction
items.body: Consignee details, pricing and contract terms are redacted or tokenised before anything crosses a boundary it shouldn't.

items.title: Full audit trail
items.body: Every question, answer, source document and escalation is logged — so a disputed answer can always be reconstructed.

items.title: Deploy where your policy requires
items.body: Your cloud account, a private VPC, or on-premise where regulation or a customer contract demands it.

items.title: Role-aware access
items.body: The agent only ever sees and reveals what the person asking is already entitled to see in your systems.

faq.heading: The things operators ask us first

items.q: Do we have to replace our TMS or WMS?
items.a: No — and we'd advise against it. Everything we build sits alongside the systems you already run and talks to them through APIs, webhooks or a read replica. Replacing a working TMS is a multi-year project; this is a matter of weeks.

items.q: How long before something is actually live?
items.a: A pilot workflow is typically in front of real users within two to four weeks. Full integration and rollout across channels usually adds another four to eight, depending on how accessible your systems are.

items.q: Won't the AI just make things up?
items.a: That is the failure mode we design against first. Answers are retrieved from your own records and cited, the agent is constrained to say "I don't know" rather than guess, and anything outside its confidence threshold escalates to a human. We also build evaluation sets so accuracy is measured, not assumed.

items.q: Can it handle Arabic as well as English?
items.a: Yes. Bilingual English–Arabic handling on phone, chat and documents is standard for GCC operations, and other languages can be added as your lanes require.

The audit call is free. Pilots are fixed-fee against a defined success metric, so you know the number before you commit. Full builds are scoped after the pilot, and ongoing monitoring and tuning is a monthly retainer.

items.q: What do you need from us to start?
items.a: For the audit, a conversation is enough. For a pilot: sample data for the workflow in question, a technical contact who knows your systems, and one operations person who lives the problem daily.
